TRIAGE DIRECTIVE (operator ruling 2026-10-03): this is an IMPLEMENTATION CHORE. Its specification and design are settled and accepted: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/ (merged as 7f0aa4ad, council-cleared in run build-decision-0065-slice-two-co-50ef1e34) and decision 0077 (accepted). Do not re-specify or re-design: classify it `chore` so it goes straight to implement. It is still reviewed by the full engine council. If the settled design cannot be implemented as written, the implement seat reports blocked; triage does not reopen the design.

BUILD DECISION 0065, SLICE TWO — UNIT U8f, one narrow visit, ONE pull request. Branch s2/U8f, cut from main at 2095773e. Recipe claude-flash-dsh-adv.

READ FIRST: design.md's "Slice two units" preamble and your unit (below, verbatim), the tasks your unit closes in tasks.md, the spec deltas it names, operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, decision 0077 and decision 0065. Units before yours in your row's Dependencies have landed on main.

THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U8f | U8e | Expose retained evidence in the pure view; 43.1–43.2 | `crates/brokkr-view/src/capability_calls.rs`; `crates/brokkr-view/src/lib.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U8f — Expose retained evidence in the pure view

Extend the consumed pure call projection with the settled checkpoint's digest/provenance, without stage assembly, path reads or derived grants.

Closes tasks 43.1 and 43.2; requirements [CC2](specs/capability-call-checkpoints/spec.md), [CR5](specs/capability-response-retention/spec.md).
Proof: Exact historical-unrecorded/no-digest/recorded distinctions and shared display values for every settled outcome; no inferred retention veto.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-view/src/tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_artifacts.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS UNIT (the-forge-67, 2026-10-06). It clarifies the commission.

Carried LOW from U4g's council (PR #562, run 0065-slice-two-unit-u4g-see-the--49c23bb2; correctness and spec-compliance, decision 0071 rulings 3/5). You own crates/brokkr-view/src/capability_calls.rs:
- The five call-state spellings are defined separately in three places: through serde, CallState::of and CallState::word (about :26-56).
- The attribution group is extracted from Value by string key (about :86-97).
- Fix: consolidate the vocabulary into one definition, and parse the group once into a type.
- Preserve the exact serialization, and preserve absence for a missing field, an empty field, and an unknown state (including a broker's private `started`). U4g's tests already bind these.

A LOW you can't fix inside your files: record it and do NOT report blocked.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U8f.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Framing: .forge/tasks/u8f-retained-evidence.md. The operator explicitly rules U8f an implementation chore under the accepted slice-two design and decision 0077, retaining full engine-council review. Tasks 43.1–43.2 extend an existing consumed pure-view projection within two named production files; the carried LOW fixes fit capability_calls.rs (decision 0071 rulings 3/5), with purity and shared derivation governed by rulings 1/7. No implementation changes or test suites were run.

U8f is built in a signed commit, b5bc6e98 (G), on s2/U8f from 2095773e. The only production file changed is crates/brokkr-view/src/capability_calls.rs. lib.rs is unchanged because its consumer, CheckpointRow's call_evidence, already carries the new field.

What changed: CallEvidence gains a `response` Cell, derived once in the view and serialized through inspect --json. It reads one of three ways. If the checkpoint has no whole v6 group, the cell is absent with UNRECORDED. An attributed call of any settled outcome without a digest is absent with CR5's 'no retained response is recorded for this call' (new pub const NO_RETAINED); it infers no veto, grant or delivery, and a refused call stays refused. A succeeded or failed call with a digest carries the digest. The view reads no path, assembles no stage and merges no rows.

The U4g LOWs are fixed (0071 rulings 3 and 5). CallState::word is the only spelling of the states, written by a hand-written Serialize, because the layering scanner refused the type string serde(into) needs. The group is parsed once via CapabilityCall::deserialize over the checkpoint, with no string-key reads. The serialized form is unchanged, and U4g's tests pass unedited, except that the historical CLI test's expected object gains the response cell.

Assumption: the provenance named in 43.1 is the call's existing capability, dialect, tool and call_id, so no second provenance type was added.

Public API growth needs the operator's ruling at PR time: CallEvidence::response, capability_calls::NO_RETAINED, and a Deserialize impl on CapabilityCall. That impl reads the journal's call_state but serializes as state, so it is asymmetric by design.

Tests: three new view tests and one new CLI test, plus the extended historical CLI test. All are bound by compiling mutations; the failing lines are recorded in evidence/U8f.md.

Gates observed on this tree: brokkr-view suite, brokkr-cli lib, it (760) and other test binaries, brokkr-runtime lib and it, fmt, workspace clippy -D warnings, recipes/self compile, openspec validate --strict, typos, git diff --check, and the quality ratchet's files and clones modes. The first full run of the it binary failed layering::scan on the serde(into) attribute; it was fixed and the whole binary then passed.

Pending: the exact-coverage gate, the macOS legs, and the capability_launch binary (not run; it does not read view call evidence). A full single `cargo test --workspace` was not run; I ran the touched and dependent crates suite by suite instead.

members.adversarial: Adversarial security review of b5bc6e98 against 2095773e. The only production file is pure brokkr-view/src/capability_calls.rs, beside its tests, one CLI integration test, tasks.md and the new U8f evidence. No journal write, seal, fence, broker, grant or refusal logic changed, and the view still reads no path and admits nothing (decision 0071 ruling 7). The parse fails closed: a missing, empty or wrongly typed group field, or any state outside the five-word v6 vocabulary (including the broker's private 'started'), makes the whole group unrecorded, never a partial call; a bad digest drops only the digest, as before. A refused call stays Refused, and NO_RETAINED says only that no digest is recorded, inferring no veto, grant or delivery (CR5). Re-ran brokkr-view's capability_calls (5/5) and brokkr-cli's it capability_artifacts:: (3/3): green. Two info-level, tamper-only observations, neither a new capability nor a weakened refusal. INFO 1: serde_json's derived-struct deserializer also accepts a JSON array positionally, so a non-object checkpoint supplied by tampering with the journal (Store::load verifies the chain, not the seat record) could now read as an attributed call where the old key lookup read it unrecorded; the same tamperer could plant the object form, so this is robustness, not a new tamper path. INFO 2: the response cell paints the journal's digest string verbatim without a 64-lowercase-hex shape check, as the other journal-derived cells do; the engine is the v6 fence's only writer and the same string was already exposed by CallEvidence.call.response_sha256, so no new secret or model prose reaches a surface. No finding above low, so no security-hold.
members.correctness: Correctness review of b5bc6e98 (U8f). The change matches its framing. CallEvidence gains a `response` cell that keeps three cases apart. A row with no whole v6 group is absent with UNRECORDED. An attributed call that cites no digest is absent with NO_RETAINED, which is CR5's exact words and infers no veto or grant; a refused call stays refused. A cited digest carries the digest. The view does no path reads, stage assembly or grant lookup (ruling 1, CR5). The U4g LOWs are fixed: CallState::word is the only spelling, used by a hand-written Serialize and by `of` through ALL (ruling 5). The group is parsed once by CapabilityCall::deserialize, and no field is read by string key any more (ruling 3). The old absence semantics hold: an empty field or an unknown/`started` state fails the whole group, and a bad digest costs only the digest. U4g's exact tests pass unedited apart from the added response cell. I re-ran brokkr-view's capability_calls (5/5) and brokkr-cli's `it capability_artifacts::` (3/3), both green, and git diff --check is clean. The new tests assert exact Cells and wire JSON, and the mutation table in evidence/U8f.md is plausible for each. Only the two production files in scope plus tests and evidence moved; lib.rs was not edited. INFO 1 (ruling 6): CapabilityCall now derives a public Deserialize that reads `call_state` but serializes `state`, so the type cannot round-trip its own wire form. Its only consumer is call_evidence, so a private parse shape or a documented note would be tidier. INFO 2: a derived struct Deserialize also accepts a JSON array positionally, which `checkpoint.get(key)` never did. Checkpoints are always objects, so this is unreachable in practice. INFO 3: public API growth (CallEvidence.response, NO_RETAINED) is recorded in the evidence for the operator's ruling at PR time, as the rules require. INFO 4: the exact-coverage gate and the macOS legs are pending until CI runs them, as the evidence states. No security concern.
members.security: Security review of b5bc6e98 against 2095773e. The diff touches only brokkr-view/src/capability_calls.rs (pure, no I/O), its tests, one CLI integration test, tasks.md and evidence/U8f.md. No journal write path, seal, broker, grant or refusal logic changed. The view still admits nothing (ruling 7). A refused call stays CallState::Refused, and the tests bind that it never reads as a grant. A missing digest yields NO_RETAINED, which says only that no digest is recorded: no veto, grant or delivery is inferred (CR5). The parse fails closed: a missing, empty or wrongly typed group field, or a state outside the five-word v6 vocabulary (including the broker's private 'started'), makes the whole group unrecorded, never a partial call. A bad digest drops only the digest. No secrets, model prose or host paths reach the journal or the evidence file. INFO 1: CapabilityCall::deserialize(&Value) goes through serde_json's struct deserializer, which also accepts a JSON array positionally. A non-object EffectCheckpointed checkpoint like [cap, dialect, tool, id, 'succeeded', digest] would now read as attributed, where the old key lookup read it as unrecorded. It can only be reached by tampering with the journal, and that same tamperer could plant the object form anyway, so there is no new tamper capability. It is a robustness gap: a type-check of Value::Object before deserializing, or #[serde(deserialize_with)] on a map-only wrapper, would close it. INFO 2: the new response cell prints the journal's digest string verbatim, without a hex-64 shape check. This matches how the model, effort and tool cells already paint journal strings, and the engine is the digest's only writer. Neither note weakens a refusal or opens a fail-open path.
